comment: src/Quadrants.cpp at commit b90cd69. The quadrant number is built at line 113 as (x >= 5V) | (y >= 5V) << 1, so A is low X and low Y, B high X and low Y, C low X and high Y, D high X and high Y; with the Y axis growing downwards, as it does on RGB Matrix and RAM-40964, that puts A top left, B top right, C bottom left and D bottom right, which is how the panel's four coloured blocks are arranged. The sixteen quadrant inputs carry no family because the module passes on whatever is patched, and nor do the four routed outputs. The four polarity switches are read per quadrant, so each quadrant can hand its coordinate back in a different range. A fault worth knowing: with either the X or the Y jack unpatched, no quadrant is worked out for channel 0, but line 139 still reads it, so the four quadrant lamps and the four gate channels follow uninitialised memory until both jacks are patched.
